paper.title: The $2D$ nonlinear shallow water equations with a partially immersed obstacle

original_title_field: The $2D$ nonlinear shallow water equations with a partially immersed obstacle
outcome: Three confirmed substantive statement/proof failures and two local corrections
summary: Theorem5 printed uniform extra boundary derivative is falsified by a smooth fully compatible subcritical high-frequency family. Proposition16's construction drops g1 and has inconsistent sign, failing even a stationary smooth example. Eq45 and Proposition6 fail for a smooth boundary pulse satisfying weak dissipativity; a corrected estimate is proved. Intended local existence/uniqueness not refuted.

P2 disproves the displayed correction construction, not Proposition16 existential statement. Corrected full compatible approximation proof not certified.
P3 disproves abstract energy inequality and proves a sufficient repaired estimate; full propagation through every downstream constant not certified and no nonlinear LWP counterexample asserted.
External hyperbolic existence, elliptic regularity and Sobolev results were not all independently reproved or downloaded.
Bounded supplement/code/correction search found no applicable separate item; this is not proof of absence and no code-absence defect.

problems.title: False uniform extra boundary derivative in Theorem5
problems.location: PDF15 Wb definition; PDF56-57 equations133-136 and Theorem5 final bound; PDF60-61 actual proof norm
problems.claim: Uniform bound of d_tan psi in W_b^(m+1/2) depending only on c0,M0.
assumptions: Smooth unit disk, hi=H0=g=1, zeta_w0 satisfyingAssumption1
problems.proof:
## P1: Theorem 5, PDF57: false uniform extra boundary derivative
The membership statement u in W^m and psi in W_b^{m+1/2} is distinct from the last displayed bound on d_tan psi in W_b^{m+1/2}. The latter requires at time zero ||d_tan psi||_{H^{m+1/2}}, although the initial-data bound controls only H^{m-1/2}. This observation alone is not the counterexample: compatibility must also hold.

Take the interior unit disk, exterior r>1, H0=hi=g=1, zeta_w=0, m=3, c0=1/4. The Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator is Lambda=|D_theta|. For fixed small delta>0 and integer n>=2 let
psi=delta*n^(-7/2)*cos(n theta), p=Lambda psi, q=psi_theta.
Then p'=nq, q'=-np and p^2+q^2 is constant. Specify the initial polar jets at r=1 by
phi=psi, phi_r=p, phi_rr=0, phi_rrr=d;
zeta=0, zeta_r=a, zeta_rr=0;
a=(n-1)(p^2-q^2)/(1+p^2).
Set v=grad phi; the data are irrotational and match the boundary potential and tangential velocity.

Write primes for theta derivatives and define
D=p+q', Z=-D-ap, U=-a-q p'+q^2,
Zr0=-aD-(-p+p''-2q')-a'q,
W=-3q^2+4q p'-(p')^2, V=-Z-pU,
Remainder=-(1+p^2)Zr0-2pW-pZD-pqZ'+[2Z-p(1+a)]U-qU'-Lambda V,
d=-Remainder/(1+3p^2).

Generate the initial time jets from
zeta_t=-div((1+zeta)grad phi), phi_t=-zeta-|grad phi|^2/2.
For G=(1+zeta)phi_r-Lambda(phi|Gamma), direct polar differentiation gives
G=0,
G_t=(n-1)(p^2-q^2)-(1+p^2)a=0,
G_tt=(1+3p^2)d+Remainder=0.
Thus all required compatibility conditions of orders 0,1,2 hold. Details useful for checking the second derivative:
zeta_tr=Zr0-d; phi_trr=W-pd;
phi_ttr=(1+p^2)d-Zr0-pW-qU';
zeta_tt=2pd-ZD-pZr0-qZ'-W-(1+a)U.
Also phi_t|Gamma=-(p^2+q^2)/2 is constant, so its first and second tangential derivatives vanish. Substitution into
G_tt=zeta_tt*p+2*Z*U+phi_ttr-Lambda(phi_tt|Gamma)
proves the displayed identity. The boundary potential time jets agree with the recursion in equation (134).

Primary independent symbolic check: boundary_jet_symbolic_check.py, actual process 72732, exit 0. It directly differentiates the polar PDE, verifies the first compatibility identity, both tangential cancellations, the coefficient 1+3p^2 of d, the full remainder, and the final zero. Its exact output is boundary_jet_symbolic_result.json. This is self-written check code, not author code. The auxiliary's different exploratory failed general-K guess is not used.

Uniform extension and norms:
For collar coordinate s=r-1 choose chi in C_c^\infty([0,infinity)), identically 1 near 0. For prescribed normal jets g_j, j=0,...,k-1, set
E_k(g)(s,theta)=sum_j s^j/j! chi(s <D_theta>)g_j(theta).
Every positive derivative of chi vanishes at 0, so the specified jets are exact. Fourier Parseval and the substitution s -> s<n> give
||E_k(g)||_{H^k} <= C sum_j ||g_j||_{H^{k-j-1/2}}.
The support lies in one fixed collar; its norm in polar geometry is equivalent to the flat collar norm. Smooth jets give smooth data that extend by zero across the outer collar edge.

Here p,q are uniformly bounded by C delta in H^{5/2}; a is bounded by C delta^2 in H^{3/2}. D,Z lie in H^{3/2}, U lies in H^{3/2}, Zr0,W and the full remainder lie in H^{1/2}, with norm O(delta)+O(delta^2)+higher powers. In particular the leading p'' term has amplitude delta*n^{-1/2} and H^{1/2} norm O(delta). Multiplication by H^{3/2} functions acts boundedly on H^{1/2}; Lambda:H^{3/2}->H^{1/2}; smooth composition with 1/(1+p^2) and 1/(1+3p^2) preserves these uniform bounds. Thus ||d||_{H^{1/2}}<=C delta.
Apply E_4 to (psi,p,0,d) and E_3 to (0,a,0):
||phi||_{H^4}+||zeta||_{H^3}<=C delta uniformly n.
Consequently ||(zeta,v)||_{H^3}+||psi_theta||_{H^{5/2}}<=M0 with one fixed M0. Two-dimensional Sobolev embedding and small fixed delta imply 1+zeta-|v|^2>=1/2=2c0 throughout the exterior. All data are smooth and compactly supported except the fixed depth.
But ||psi_theta||_{H^{7/2}} is comparable to delta*n and diverges. The printed uniform bound is therefore false already at t=0 under every stated hypothesis.

Impact: a main theorem's uniform regularity conclusion is false; intended existence, uniqueness and the membership in equation (136) are not refuted. Repair: use the lower boundary derivative norm actually controlled in the proof, or explicitly sum ||d_tan partial_t^j psi||_{H^{m-j-1/2}}, j=0,...,m. Simply removing d_tan and bounding the full psi norm with the same M0 is not valid without fixing the additive gauge: M0 does not control the constant mode of psi. Proposed severity Major by actual main-conclusion damage, not by irreparability.
counterevidence_checked: Compatibility not ignored; Gtt full remainder and coefficient checked analytically and rootSympyexit0
No invocation disputed existence theorem to construct initialdata
Cannot simply remove dtan without controlling gauge

problems.correction: Use actual lower mixed boundary energy seminorm; control gauge separately for full potential norm.
problems.repair_verification: Lowerorder norm consistentwith energyproof; fullrepaired theorem not independently reproved.

check.independent_reasoning: Root read Theorem5 and its exact compatibility recursion, then reconstructed G_t=(n-1)(p^2-q^2)-(1+p^2)a and the coefficient1+3p^2 of the third normal jet in G_tt. Choosing a and d as in the report enforces all three required orders for m=3. The explicit Fourier collar extension controls bulk H3 and d_tan psi H5/2 uniformly, and fixed small delta enforces strict subcriticality. Yet d_tan psi H7/2 grows delta*n at t=0. Thus the uniform quantitative conclusion is false under the actual hypotheses, without using the disputed existence theorem to construct data. Existence/uniqueness and the membership statement are not disproved; constant-mode gauge must be accounted for in any full-potential repair.

problems.title: Proposition16 compatible-data correction omits nonhomogeneous boundary source
problems.claim: Displayed correction yields compatible approximate data with correction tendingtozero for generalg1.
problems.proof:
## P2: Proposition 16, PDF52: missing inhomogeneous compatibility data and sign
Equation (110), PDF48, requires N.u_j^II=Lambda psi_j+(partial_t^j g1)(0). Proposition16 defines w=u_new-u_tilde and phi=psi_tilde-psi_new, but uses a recursion with the sign appropriate to phi=psi_new-psi_tilde. Its displayed normal correction also omits the g1 jet. No earlier homogenization applies: Theorem4 Step2, PDF54, explicitly treats general g1^(n).

A full smooth counterexample to this construction uses the same disk, hi=1, S=I3. Let chi(r)=1 near r=1 and 0 for r>=2, smoothly. Set
u=(0,chi(r)e_r), psi=0,
f=(chi'(r)+chi(r)/r,0,0), g1=1, g2=0.
This is a stationary solution of (103)-(105), has all Sobolev regularities used there, and satisfies compatibility to every order. Take all approximations identical to the original data and u_tilde^in=u^in. The correct correction is zero.
The printed j=0 formula instead forces N.w_0^II=-1. Hence the corrected normal trace becomes 0 rather than the required 1; the correction cannot converge to zero in H^m, by the trace theorem. The claimed residual convergence to zero is also false: its uncorrected residual equals g1=1.

Repair: define phi=psi_new-psi_tilde and use
N.w_j^II=Lambda phi_j+g1_j^(n)-(N.u_tilde_j^II-Lambda psi_tilde_j).
Then this example has zero correction. Every jet, sign and extension must be carried through the amended construction. This is a counterexample to the proof's construction, not to Proposition16's existence assertion (which this example trivially satisfies).
Dependency: Proposition16 supplies Theorem4 Step2's compatible smooth approximations; the general linear theory is then used for the differentiated nonlinear boundary problem, including nonzero commutator boundary sources. Proposed Major for a failed core proof construction; repairability does not automatically make it Minor.
problems.correction: Use phi=new-minus-tilde and include g1_j in residual; propagateallsigns/jets.

check.independent_reasoning: The root read the actual Proposition16 correction and verified the stationary disk example. Equal approximations of u=(0,chi e_r), psi=0, f=(chi'+chi/r,0,0), g1=1, g2=0 satisfy every time compatibility condition; the displayed j=0 correction nevertheless imposes N.w=-1 and destroys the required trace. The omitted g1 and the reversed phi convention are genuine errors in the construction supplying Theorem4 and the nonlinear approximation. Zero correction solves the example, so no existential impossibility is asserted. The proposed amended residual is checked, not the complete repaired construction.

problems.title: Final signed boundary flux cannot control past supremum energy
problems.proof:
## P3: Equation (45), PDF21, and Proposition6, PDF22
A peak-in-time norm cannot be controlled by the final cumulative signed boundary flux with the coefficients printed there.

Let E={r>1}, scalar unknown, S=1, zero-order B=0, f=0, T*=1/100,
b=T*/(8pi), s(t)=-2b cos(2pi t/T*), a(t)=s'(t)=sin(2pi t/T*)/2,
A_j=a(t)x_j/r.
Then |a|<=1/2 and div A=a/r<=1/2. All Assumption2 conditions hold with alpha0=beta0=beta0in=beta1=1. In particular no bound on A_t is imposed by that assumption or Proposition6.
For a nonzero eta in C_c^\infty(-b,b), set u(t,x)=eta(r-1-s(t)).
Direct differentiation gives u_t+A.grad u=0. The solution and its boundary trace g_b are smooth, with u(0)=u(T*)=0 and nonzero interior energy at intermediate times.
Define, for every lambda>=1,
S_data(t)=int_0^t e^{-2lambda tau} int_Gamma a_+ |g_b|^2,
E_bdry(t)=int_0^t e^{-2lambda tau} int_Gamma a_- |u|^2.
Both are nonnegative, S_data is nondecreasing and depends only on the prescribed boundary data and coefficients. The boundary flux is exactly S_data-E_bdry, so Definition2 holds, even without its permitted bulk remainder. Its lambda dependence is the same as the paper's Examples2,3.

Set lambda=1, E(t)=||u(t)||_2^2, M=max e^{-2t}E(t)>0. The exterior outward normal is -e_r, so direct integration by parts gives
E'(t)=int_Gamma a u^2+int_E (a/r)u^2.
With both endpoint energies zero,
F=int_0^{T*} e^{-2t} int_Gamma a u^2
 =int_0^{T*} e^{-2t} int_E (2-a/r)u^2 <=(5/2)T*M.
Definition (28) gives I_{1,T*}(||u||)^2>=M.
Equation (45) with zero initial/body data gives I^2<=4F<=M/10, false.
Proposition6 gives I^2<=8(S_data-E_bdry)=8F<=M/5, false.
This analytic counterexample satisfies all of their stated assumptions and is not a numerical conjecture.

Verified repair:
Let J=I_lambda,t((Su,u)^{1/2}), A=(S(0)u0,u0),
B=sqrt(beta0) S*_lambda,t(||f||).
The endpoint energy estimate for lambda>=beta1/alpha0, with Definition2 substituted BEFORE taking a time supremum, bounds
X=sup e^{-2lambda tau}(Su,u)(tau) and
Y+E_bdry(t)=lambda int e^{-2lambda tau}(Su,u)+E_bdry(t)
separately by Q=A+2BJ+S_data(t)+J^2/8.
Thus J^2+2E_bdry<=4Q, since J^2=(sqrt(X)+sqrt(Y))^2<=2(X+Y).
Rearrange and use 8BJ<=J^2/4+64B^2 to obtain
J^2+8E_bdry<=16A+256B^2+16S_data.
Therefore a valid replacement is
I_u^2+(8/alpha0)E_bdry
 <=16(beta0in/alpha0)||u0||^2
  +256(beta0/alpha0)(S*||f||)^2
  +(16/alpha0)S_data.
No extra regularity, derivatives or monotonicity of E_bdry are required.
Impact: the foundational weak-dissipation estimate and its inference as printed are false. The qualitative energy control admits a direct correction. Subsequent estimates with unspecified C(K0) may absorb it; no specific nonlinear LWP counterexample follows. Severity must track this failed core energy step and be distinguished from a refutation of the nonlinear theorem.

check.independent_reasoning: Root re-read the signed flux inequality and weak-dissipation quantifiers. For the smooth radial pulse, u_t+a u_r=0, initial and final fields vanish, and |a|<=1/2 with divA<=1/2 meets the stated coefficient hypotheses. With exterior normal -e_r, E'=boundary(a u^2)+bulk(a/r u^2). Hence the final weighted flux is <=(5/2)T*M, although the past-supremum norm is >=M>0. T=1/100 contradicts both printed factors4 and8. The prescribed-boundary positive/negative flux split meets Definition2; no unlisted A_t assumption is introduced. Inserting weak dissipativity before the supremum gives the report's explicit16/256/16 replacement constants. This is a core energy failure, not a nonlinear nonexistence result.

problems.title: Pressure-density and fixed interior energy normalization
problems.proof:
## P4: local normalization identities, PDF4 and31
Take I the unit disk, H0=2, hi=1, zeta_w=-1, g=1, rho=2, P_atm=0, zeta=0, v=v_i=0, P_i=2, phi=psi=0. Positive depths, stationary PDE, mass/tangent matching, all compatibility and strict subcriticality hold.
The correct physical pressure relation used in the main body is P_i+rho*g*zeta_w=0, and is satisfied. Introductory equation(3), PDF4, omits rho and asserts instead 0=P_i+g*zeta_w=1. Correct by dividing the pressures by rho, or multiplying gravitational and kinetic terms by rho. The main-body convention, PDF8, is consistent; no extra core failure established.
On PDF31, the reduced potential energy omits the fixed interior term (g/2) int_I zeta_w^2. For the same data E_reduced=0 but E_physical/rho=pi/2. Equality requires this additive constant or a stated zero-of-energy convention. Time conservation is unaffected. Minor, grouped as two normalization discrepancies with the same explicit admissible equilibrium.

check.independent_reasoning: The stationary disk with rho2, zeta_w=-1 and P_i2 satisfies the body Bernoulli balance P_i+rho*g*zeta_w=0; the introductory missing-rho expression gives1. Its reduced energy is0 but physical energy/rho is pi/2. The body convention and time derivative of the fixed interior constant are correct; no additional central failure follows.

problems.title: Inverse-eigenvalue list includes an unconstrained first-block eigenvalue
problems.claim: Ass6liststarts lambda_n1^-1 although nonzero block starts n1+1.
problems.proof: The first n1 eigenvalues are not assumed to be bounded away from zero. Example5 on PDF27 permits lambda1=N.v, which need not vanish. In the actual Corollary2 application (PDF39), n1=1, n2=2 and (lambda1,lambda2,lambda3)=(0,1,-1). Assumption6 as printed therefore requests the reciprocal of zero, whereas Lemma3 divides only by lambda_j for j=n1+1,...,n. The reciprocal list should start at n1+1. This is an assumption/application mismatch, not a counterexample to the theorem conditional on its stronger written assumptions.
counterevidence_checked: Example5 permits a nonzero first-block eigenvalue; no claim that the whole first block is identically zero remains.

check.independent_reasoning: Root checked Assumptions5-6, Example5, Lemma3 and the actual Corollary2 application. The first block is not generally zero: Example5 has lambda1=N.v. The actual transformed application has eigenvalues0,1,-1 and n1=1, so the printed reciprocal list requires1/0. Lemma3 already divides only on j>=n1+1. Findings and its per-claim evidence are corrected to this precise scope; the current TeX already states this correctly and remains unchanged.
